clue.text: At home chasing criminal, good example of 28

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the home word follows the criminal

parts.note: a hood is a gangster or criminal
at home means in

explanation.surface: Police at someone's house are pursuing a crook, a fine instance of something cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 is the answer to 28-across, a word for cruel treatment; covering a prisoner's head with a hood is a recognised interrogation abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a bag over a detainee's head is a notorious form of abuse used in interrogations.

clue.text: Old ass pulled up aromatic plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulled up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an onager is a wild ass of Asia

explanation.surface: An elderly donkey was tugged upward by its handler, by a fragrant herb.
explanation.definitionFit: This culinary herb, related to marjoram, is a fragrant plant used in Mediterranean cooking.

clue.text: Rear gunner seized by complete terror

indicators.note: seized by means held inside, so the gunner's letter goes within the other word

parts.note: dead can mean complete, as in a dead loss or dead certainty

indicators.note: rear points to the back end of the word gunner, its final letter

explanation.surface: A tail gunner on a bomber is gripped by absolute fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name great fear; dread is a synonym for terror.

clue.text: Eccentric uncle has a right to form basic kind of family

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so these letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: An odd uncle is entitled to set up a household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' shuffles UNCLE plus A and R into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear family is the basic unit of parents and children only, without wider relatives.

clue.text: Name of retired boxing trainer's last heavyweight champ

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so one piece goes around the other
retired means drawn back, so the words name and of are read backwards
last picks the final letter of the word trainer's

explanation.surface: A trainer names the old champion of the heavyweight division who has stopped fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport but means enclosing: the reversed pair FOEMAN wraps the R that ends 'trainer's'. George Foreman retired from the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: George Foreman was twice world heavyweight boxing champion, so he is an example of such a titleholder.

clue.text: Ignoring eccentric Victorian conservationist's unusual beginnings

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the letters of the second word are taken away
eccentric signals the removed word's letters may be scattered in any order
unusual means out of the ordinary, so what remains is rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter; this word supplies the pool of letters
this word's letters are the ones discarded from the pool

explanation.surface: A quirky nineteenth-century nature lover had strange early days.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of VICTORIAN from CONSERVATIONIST, leaving O N S E S T; 'unusual' then rearranges these.
explanation.definitionFit: Starts or commencements are beginnings, as in the first appearance of an illness or season.

clue.text: Will woman almost kill bloke who was farcical in the bedroom?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to execute is to put to death

parts.words: bloke who was farcical in the bedroom
parts.note: Brian Rix starred in British bedroom farces at the Whitehall Theatre, famously losing his trousers

explanation.surface: A determined woman nearly murders a man known for comic bedroom scenes?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will woman' looks like a determined woman, but means a woman named in a will to carry it out. Brian Rix was a British actor-manager of trouser-dropping farces.
explanation.definitionFit: An executrix is the female executor of a will, administering the estate of the deceased.

clue.text: School show doesn't start well!

indicators.note: doesn't start means losing the opening letter of the word for show

parts.note: a facade is an outward show or pretence
my! is an exclamation of surprise like well!

explanation.surface: A school's performance gets off to a bad beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' is not a performance but a facade, a false front; drop its first letter for ACADE.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a type of school, especially one specialising in a field or a state-funded English school.

clue.text: Obama dispatched top agony aunt to reorganise detention facility

indicators.note: to reorganise means to rearrange, so the combined letters are mixed up
dispatched top means the first letter has been sent away

parts.note: taken as written; an agony aunt writes an advice column

explanation.surface: The president sacked a senior advice columnist to restructure a prison camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispatched top' removes the O at the head of OBAMA, leaving BAMA, which 'to reorganise' shuffles with AGONY AUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: The US runs a notorious military prison for terror suspects at this naval base in Cuba.

clue.text: Report grain yield

indicators.note: report means something spoken, so the word is said out loud

parts.note: a seed is a grain of a cereal plant

explanation.surface: A news bulletin on the harvest of cereal crops.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield territory or a point is to give it up, which is what ceding means.

clue.text: Cadets up to mischief in putsches

indicators.note: mischief means playful trouble-making, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Trainee officers are misbehaving during military uprisings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up to' seems to belong to 'up to mischief', but both words are fodder with CADETS.
explanation.definitionFit: A putsch is a sudden violent seizure of power, the same thing as a French-style overthrow.

clue.text: Short comic villain

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: David Baddiel is a British comedian

explanation.surface: A pint-sized comedian plays the bad guy.
explanation.walkthrough: David Baddiel is an English stand-up comedian and writer; trim his surname by its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A baddie is an informal word for the bad guy or villain of a story.

clue.text: Knesset arranged to import uranium for Japanese fixers

indicators.note: to import means to bring in, so the element symbol is placed inside
arranged means put into order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Israel's parliament set up a deal to bring in nuclear fuel for Japanese mechanics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knesset' is the Israeli parliament, its letters shuffled by 'arranged'.
explanation.definitionFit: Netsuke are small carved Japanese toggles used to fasten pouches to a kimono sash, hence fixers.

clue.text: Bodily ingestion of drug by soldier

indicators.note: ingestion means swallowing, so the soldier takes in the drug

parts.note: a corporal is a non-commissioned soldier
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A serviceman swallowing narcotics, in a physical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporeal means relating to the body as opposed to the spirit; a synonym of bodily.

clue.text: Pop star and model exploit it

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A singer and a catwalk model take advantage of the situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a second person beside the pop star, but is the verb signalling the anagram of EXPLOIT IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pixie Lott is an English singer who had chart-topping hits around 2009.

clue.text: Criminal brothers' utter madness

indicators.note: utter means to speak, so the word is said out loud

parts.note: a craze is a mania or madness

explanation.surface: Notorious gangster siblings displayed complete insanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utter' looks like 'complete' but is the verb 'say'. The Kray twins were infamous East London gangsters of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronnie and Reggie Kray were twin gangsters who ran organised crime in London's East End.

clue.text: Source of extremely poor quality resin

indicators.note: source of means the beginning, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: poxy is British slang for rubbishy or of poor quality

explanation.surface: Where really shoddy glue comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of extremely' looks like it qualifies 'poor', but it supplies just the E that starts 'extremely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Epoxy is a synthetic resin used in strong adhesives and coatings.

clue.text: Inactive medicine with rank smell

parts.note: a place is a position or rank, as in first place
BO is short for body odour, a smell

explanation.surface: An ineffective drug that smells terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like an adjective meaning foul-smelling, but it is a noun for position.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy pill with no active ingredient, given as a control or for reassurance.

clue.text: Indulging in every type of eroticism, especially in the kitchen?

definitions.text: Indulging in every type of eroticism, especially in the kitchen?

parts.words: Indulging in every type of eroticism, especially in the kitchen
parts.note: a word for attraction to all genders, playfully read as attraction to cooking pots and pans

explanation.surface: Someone who is up for anything sexually, particularly among the cooking utensils.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix pan- means all, so this describes attraction regardless of sex or gender; the kitchen joke reads it as pot-loving.

clue.text: South's long associated with an extremely immoral institution

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south
L is an abbreviation for long, as in longitude
very means extremely

explanation.surface: The southern states were long linked with a deeply wicked system.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the American South, where the answer was in fact entrenched.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning people as property is the immoral system once established across many societies.

clue.text: An ancestor's spirit causing astonishment

parts.note: an becomes the indefinite article a
ma, mother, is an ancestor; the possessive adds no letter
zing means energy or spirit

explanation.surface: The ghost of a forebear produces wonder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests a ghost, but here means liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something astounding causes astonishment, which is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Arachne became this reclusive hispid eremite

indicators.note: reclusive means withdrawn from view, so the word lies tucked inside these words

explanation.surface: The setter turned into this bristly hermit.
explanation.walkthrough: Arachne is both the setter's pseudonym and the weaver of Greek myth whom Athena turned into an eight-legged creature. Hispid means bristly.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth Athena transformed the mortal weaver Arachne into a web-spinning creature.

clue.text: Confront effrontery with angry pout

parts.note: face means cheek or effrontery, as in having the face to do something

indicators.note: angry means agitated, so these letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Challenge someone's cheek with a cross sulky look.
explanation.definitionFit: To face up to a problem is to confront it bravely rather than avoid it.

clue.text: Sensual Lana Turner embracing single male

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the other letters go within
a turner is something that turns, so the name Lana is turned backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: The sultry film star Lana Turner hugs an unmarried man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lana Turner' reads as the Hollywood actress; 'Turner' turns LANA into ANAL, which 'embracing' wraps around I and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal as an adjective means relating to physical, carnal appetites, so it fits sensual.

clue.text: Republicans getting counter-intelligence from Baghdad?

parts.note: the IRA, the Irish Republican Army, are republicans

indicators.note: counter means running the opposite way, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: IQ is a measure of intelligence

explanation.surface: Republican agents obtain spy information from the Iraqi capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter-intelligence' looks like spying, but splits into a reversal indicator and IQ.
explanation.definitionFit: Baghdad is the capital of this Middle Eastern country, so someone from there has its nationality.

clue.text: S-Class is mediocre

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for second
a rate is a class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A luxury Mercedes model is merely average.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mercedes S-Class is a top luxury car, the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of inferior quality, not the best, is mediocre.

clue.text: Antiquarian part song

indicators.note: part means a portion, so the word is a section of the longer word

explanation.surface: An ancient piece of music for several voices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part song' looks like a choral piece, but 'part' signals a section of 'Antiquarian'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera or oratorio.

clue.text: It's wrong for all to see and extremely reprehensible

definitions.text: It's wrong for all to see and extremely reprehensible

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
U is the British film rating for universal, suitable for everyone

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme ends, so the outer letters are taken

explanation.surface: A statement that cruelty is plainly wrong and deeply blameworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflicting severe pain is a wrong recognised publicly and utterly reprehensible, read as the whole clue.

clue.text: Gray's Inn, for the most part, is to be refurbished in lilac

indicators.note: refurbished means renovated, so the letters are rearranged
for the most part means not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Gray's Inn is one of the London Inns of Court for barristers

explanation.surface: Most of a London legal building is to be redecorated in a pale purple.
explanation.walkthrough: Gray's Inn is one of the four Inns of Court in London; drop its last N, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Syringa is the botanical genus name of the lilac, a flowering shrub.
